endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: (d) the AI Technologies perform in accordance with the accuracy, precision, and performance specifications set forth in the applicable SOW or documentation;

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) in vendor contracts that address incident response, response times, and availability of critical support.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: ID.SC-5: Response and recovery planning and testing are conducted with suppliers and third-party providers

commentary.bottom_line: Three governance frameworks endorse contract terms for service levels, performance warranties, and outage and disaster recovery in AI vendor agreements, but no study supplied here tests whether such terms reduce unremedied AI degradation or downtime. The recommendation currently rests on expert consensus and analogy to general IT procurement practice rather than on outcome data from health care AI deployments.

perspectives.view: No study tests the practice, and no study documents the hazard's frequency or consequences in health care AI. The support consists of three framework endorsements, one rated must and two rated should. Under GRADE conventions, expert frameworks do not count as evidence of effect, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

The endorsements come from voluntary frameworks. CHAI playbooks call for warranties that AI performs to documented accuracy and performance specifications, NIST AI 600-1 recommends SLAs covering incident response and availability, and the CHAI Assurance Standards Guide calls for recovery planning and testing with suppliers. None of these carries legal force, so contract terms remain the main enforcement mechanism.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares health systems with and without enforceable AI service and performance terms on outcomes such as downtime duration, time to remediate performance drift, vendor response times, or patient-facing disruptions. Studies are also needed that describe how often AI outages or degradation occur in clinical settings and whether contractual remedies are invoked and effective.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of the practice exists, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may have less bargaining power with vendors and less capacity for contract review, which means any benefit of these terms may be distributed unevenly, but this has not been studied.
